sections.heading: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: MXR Imaging's Platinum workflow starts at the point of purchase with a service-life review of every documented repair and replacement date across the computer, RF, gradient, patient transport, console, table, magnet, and cryo subsystems, each plotted against OEM specs and mean time between failures, before the system is de-installed, shipped, disassembled, decontaminated, reassembled, and staged for verification [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:10:09]. The replacement triggers are hard-coded: a cold head past half its life is changed automatically with OEM remanufactured parts, while one under that mark is judged on hours and performance rather than swapped for the sake of it [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:29:43]. Tubes follow the same logic, with a fairly new tube still pulled if it has been spiking or causing image-quality problems, and the whole Platinum cycle runs 90 to 120 days, CT landing on the longer side because of all the electromechanical items [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:32:21]. Block Imaging runs a comparable relay: project manager, then a cosmetic crew that sands panels, primes, re-sands, and paints, then engineering for testing, part replacement, and full calibration, then warehouse crating for safe shipping, mechanical install on site, and a final imaging-engineer calibration before handoff to service [Py7IK0wId1k @ 00:01:10].

MXR Imaging's own cost-of-ownership math shows where the margin sits. On CT, the OEM quoted 375 against an MXR price $100,000 lower, and post-warranty service ran $89,000 a year from the OEM versus $72,000 from MXR, for $185,000 saved across the first six years [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:26:06]. On MRI the spread widens: 805 from the OEM against 595 from MXR, a 210 gap on purchase, with service at $85,000 instead of $110,000 a year, adding up to $335,000 saved over six years [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:26:53]. The warranty package backing that spread covers labor and travel 8:00 to 5:00 Monday through Friday, a 30-minute phone response, six hours on site, a 96% uptime guarantee, four planned maintenance visits a year, 100% parts and MRI coil coverage, next-morning parts delivery, and 24/7 remote monitoring of the cryo subsystem [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:24:11]. Block Imaging sets the outer brackets of the market: new can cost twice as much as the other categories, used ships as-is with every bump and bruise and only adds service parts and labor coverage at extra cost, and refurbished typically carries a one-year parts and labor warranty [VOR_RnHfhE4 @ 00:01:43].

On the data-center side, Reclaim Atlas shows how the deal actually closes. In a 2026 Oak Ridge, Tennessee shutdown, a specialist pulled a 225 kVA UPS, a 180 kW standby generator, cooling gear, and racks, cleared the room in 10 days, and paid the owner $12,000, because the recovered generator and UPS could be refurbished and resold for enough to cover the removal [jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:00:13]. UPS buyers treat a 10-year-old cabinet as two assets, sending battery strings toward recycling while refurbishing the rectifiers, inverters, and controls, and they ask for model, kVA and kW, input and output voltage, age, service history, battery date codes, and matching bypass gear, since a 480 volt three-phase unit only sells to a site that can take it [jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:03:37]. Vision Matrix Institute gives the switchgear number a buyer has to match: 25 kiloamp short-time withstand is the modern default for 33 kV systems, meaning the gear survives a 25,000 amp short circuit for a full 3 seconds [6nfvCdjM9lM @ 00:04:50]. Keentel Engineering's worked example shows why the IT number alone never sizes the iron: a 500 kW IT load grows to roughly 930 kW continuous once cooling, losses, support loads, and 20% growth are added, specified as two 1,250 kW generators in N+1 [nico3vxC_dA @ 00:11:16].

callout.title: How Brokers Squeeze Value Out of Retired Imaging and Power Iron
callout.body: Field moves the practitioners use to raise sale prices, vet refurbishers, and keep resale value intact through removal and commissioning.
items: Before calling a buyer, have anyone on staff shoot a glamour shot, the series tag, the computers, and the gantry from front, back, and side; it confirms age and configuration and lets the buyer quote the best price [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:02:26].

Walk a refurbisher's floor by phone video: you should see parts, magnet farms, chillers, and cold head subassemblies, and you should ask how much inventory actually backs your warranty versus sits waiting to be reclassified [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:05:45].

Sell complete powertrains where possible: a generator moved with its transfer switch and paralleling gear preserves equipment already designed to work together and is more attractive than isolated pieces [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:07:41].
Photograph the test equipment and its calibration dates and attach them to the digital check sheet the same day, so nobody can question the results later [Broma Engineering — hukziWCxjUY @ 00:12:21].

sop_steps.title: Build the Asset Dossier
sop_steps.action: Compile year, make, model, usage counters, configuration, licensed software, and photos before contacting any buyer or seller.
sop_steps.detail: List the value drivers up front: year, make, and model, then tube age, scan seconds, and milliamp seconds, then injectors, monitoring, workstations, and software licenses [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:01:19].

sop_steps.title: Walk the Site Before Demolition Crews
sop_steps.action: Photograph nameplates, check ratings, review service records, and calculate what can come out without destroying its value.
sop_steps.detail: Specialist buyers get in ahead of demolition, then electricians shut systems down, riggers pull the equipment, and batteries split off toward recycling; careless cutting or a basement with no exit route can wipe out resale value [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:09:34].

sop_steps.title: Test to Prove Technical Identity
sop_steps.action: Load bank the generators, inspect UPS wear items and bypass, and run oil and turns ratio tests on transformers.
sop_steps.detail: Technicians check fans and capacitors, overheated connections, power modules, control boards, bypass operation, alarms, and monitoring, replacing old batteries so an old UPS returns with brand new energy storage [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:04:08].

sop_steps.title: Recondition, Stage, and Hand Off
sop_steps.action: Reassemble, test every coil and subsystem, stage the full system for verification, then ship, install, and calibrate on site.
sop_steps.detail: After the physical process the system is reassembled for testing, all coils are evaluated, reconditioned, and system tested, computer subsystems are verified, and the system is staged before it ships to its new home [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:10:55].

sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The first split is over which tier of imaging iron to buy or broker. Jordan at Block Imaging lays out three lanes: new can cost twice as much as the other categories, used ships as-is with every bump and bruise from its prior home, and refurbished sits in the middle with all components tested, calibrated to OEM specs, repainted, and backed by a 1-year parts and labor warranty. Block calls refurbished the best balance of capital outlay and system longevity [VOR_RnHfhE4 @ 00:02:46]. Jordan still concedes that a used purchase, with due diligence and add-on service coverage from a reputable provider, can be a strong value. MXR Imaging pushes its reconditioned lane harder, stating that 40 to 50% reductions from new are not uncommon at all and that every reconditioned system should carry an all-inclusive warranty of at least one year [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:06:53]. Block Imaging's acquisitions team flips the logic for sellers: a facility chasing new studies built on new isotopes, contrast agents, AI, or software has to buy new, because that capability will not surface on the secondary market [4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:00:18]. Reclaim Atlas attacks the bargain-bin stereotype, pointing to Terveystalo choosing a refurbished MRI for its Tikkurila location, with selected components and software modernized, as a deliberate investment rather than an emergency compromise [XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:01:16].

On service, the line runs between OEM loyalty and independent operators. MXR Imaging's product specialist argues the only thing separating an MXR refurb from an OEM refurb is that the OEM owns the software license and the 510k, and that otherwise MXR machines are as nice if not nicer [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:33:06]. Probo Medical UK attacks the OEM end-of-service declaration head-on: when an OEM says a system is end of service, that does not always mean end of value, and its OEM-trained engineers can often extend system life at a much lower cost than the manufacturer, without being tied to any single manufacturer's limitations [MZI2TSrdxAQ @ 00:00:58]. Reclaim Atlas applies the buyer-side brake, noting that Philips advertises warranty and service support on its circular edition MRI systems, but that this does not mean every used scanner comes with equivalent terms, so buyers must ask what is covered, which parts are excluded, and who responds when a fault appears [XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:07:52]. Wear-part policy splits as well. MXR does not swap cold heads just to swap them; a cold head past half its life is changed automatically, anything younger gets evaluated against its mean time between failures, and replacements come from OEM remanufactured stock rather than being thrown in for show [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:29:43].

On the data center power side, practitioners split over what to buy whole, what to part out, and what to spec. Reclaim Atlas argues complete powertrains can be more attractive than isolated pieces, because a generator sold with its transfer switch and paralleling gear preserves equipment already designed to work together, while assets that fail the second-life test slide down the value ladder into donor boards, power modules, breakers, and eventually copper and steel [jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:07:41]. Bridge time is the next fork. Keentel Engineering describes UPS batteries carrying the full facility load for a few minutes up to around 15, just long enough for generators to start and stabilize [kE7QqYqWub8 @ 00:03:02]. Keentel then pegs VRLA at a 3 to 5 year service life with lower upfront cost and tighter cooling needs, against lithium-ion at 10 or more years with an integrated battery management system, steering VRLA toward cost-driven or legacy installs and lithium toward space-constrained or long life cycle builds [kE7QqYqWub8 @ 00:03:19]. Vision Matrix Institute pushes the opposite edge, warning that a one-minute lithium UPS paired with generators needing 50 seconds to stabilize and take load leaves just 10 seconds between a smooth transition and total facility blackout, and asks whether the DG plant is truly designed fast enough to catch that load [6nfvCdjM9lM @ 00:12:40].

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most common imaging loss is a deal that looks cheap at quote and turns expensive at the building. Reclaim Atlas walks through a clinic that found an attractive scanner without checking its building: the equipment quote looks manageable, then the installation survey reveals additional work, and the actual project becomes a different proposition even though the advertised price never moved [XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:05:21]. The same channel warns buyers to pin down the handover point, whether seller responsibility ends when the equipment is collected, when it reaches the building, or after agreed installation tests, because headline-price shoppers miss that difference entirely and inherit the unexpected problems [XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:08:20]. Brown's Medical Imaging flags the access squeeze from the installer's side, noting crews sometimes have to strip covers just to clear challenging doorways, and that a buyer who paid for preconditioned equipment does not want beautiful covers hiding a dirty, nasty interior [DpGCQ1Ijs-Y @ 00:00:15]. MXR Imaging adds the shop-floor danger: a CT gantry spinning during a scan pulls G loading in excess of six Gs, and a CT without covers is a very dangerous machine, which is part of why CT reconditioning, with all its bearings, bushings, and adjustments, runs longer than MRI work [Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:15:37].

Data center power gear loses its resale value during extraction more often than on the quote sheet. Reclaim Atlas reports that a desirable generator can be expensive to pull without a crane, a valuable UPS can be trapped in a basement with no practical route out, and careless cutting can destroy the exact bus sections and breakers that make switchgear worth reselling, which is why specialist buyers value the removal project as well as the machine [jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:06:00]. The same channel says voltage can end the conversation quickly, because a 480 volt 3-phase UPS is only useful to a site that can accommodate it, and a bargain machine with the wrong configuration becomes expensive inventory [jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:03:53]. Broma Engineering, working the commissioning side, warns that the logistics plan has to be thought out well in advance or a transformer delivery turns into absolute chaos, with doors left off, drywall openings enlarged, and corridors cleared so nobody ends up under a landing transformer [hukziWCxjUY @ 00:03:06]. Broma also flags the RACI matrix as a delay trap: if roles between vendor, electrical contractor, CXA, general contractor, and client team are not clearly defined before the project starts, testing the transformer-to-switchboard connection gets messy and causes delays [hukziWCxjUY @ 00:08:31].

Sizing errors are the quiet money-killers on the data center side. Keentel Engineering separates two failure modes: undersizing trips protective devices on the first hot design day, while oversizing never trips but strands capital, keeps no-load losses running, and drags down PUE [nico3vxC_dA @ 00:02:12]. Keentel's case study shows a design that sized generators on average PUE and used a simplified cooling calc; the first chiller restart would have pushed the generators toward an unacceptable operating condition, forcing a resized generator plant, staggered mechanical restarts, and a corrected heat load to avoid a potentially catastrophic summer outage [nico3vxC_dA @ 00:17:52]. Vision Matrix Institute calls sizing the main incomer for day-one load a classic junior engineer trap, because 18 months later a new tenant maxes it out and a live MV panel cannot be casually swapped. The fix is blunt: always size the incomer for the absolute future design capacity of the board, not just today's initial load [6nfvCdjM9lM @ 00:04:20]. NexLayer Tech closes the loop on operations: if PSU 1 fails unnoticed and PSU 2 fails days later, a redundant system has silently become a single point of failure, which is why monitoring of load, UPS status, battery condition, generator status, and alarms is essential [o7egpgd1LLI @ 00:11:39].

callout.title: Four Checks Before Money Moves on Imaging or Power Iron
callout.body: Every item below comes from a trap a practitioner hit or watched a buyer hit. Clear all four before quoting, bidding, or releasing a deposit.
items: Before pricing any imaging system, get year, make, model, tube age, scan seconds or milliamp seconds, configuration, licensed software, and photos including the series tag, computers, and gantry front, back, and side [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:01:19].

Before paying serious money for a standby generator, pull the nameplate, kilowatt rating, voltage, fuel type, operating hours, and maintenance history, then require a load bank test so it proves it carries demand instead of merely starting and idling [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:02:49].

Before accepting a refurbished MRI, confirm every coil was system tested and ships with a signal to noise ratio sheet, and buy reconditioned gear from an ISO 13485 certified company with a documented cradle-to-grave paper trail [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:30:28].

Before signing off on generator or transformer sizing, reject average PUE math and size for the design-day peak, verifying step loading, power factor, and UPS recharge so the first chiller restart does not push the plant into an unacceptable condition [Keentel Engineering — nico3vxC_dA @ 00:17:52].

chapters.pull_quote: "When an OEM says a system is end of service, that doesn't always mean that it's end of value." Attributed to Probo Medical UK (MZI2TSrdxAQ @ 00:00:58).
action_checklist: Build a seller value-driver list before the first call: year, make, model, tube usage, accessories, injectors, workstations, licensing software, plus a glamour shot and detail photos of the series tag, computers, and gantry [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:02:10].

Vet any refurbisher by phone walkthrough of its facility, looking for parts inventory, magnet farms, chillers, and cold head subassemblies, and ask how much inventory actually backs your warranty [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:05:13].

Compare imaging offers only on comparable totals covering equipment, necessary repairs, removal, transport, site preparation, installation, and testing, then nail down the exact handover point in the contract [Reclaim Atlas — XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:07:08].

On UPS deals, collect exact model, KVA and kilowatt rating, input and output voltage, age, service history, battery date codes, and whether matching bypass or paralleling equipment is included [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:03:37].

Bundle disconnecting, rigging, and freight into data center decommission bids so recovered generator and UPS resale value pays for clearing the room, as in the Tennessee job where the owner was paid $12,000 [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:06:28].

Run the eight-step sizing workflow: IT peak load ignoring nameplates, design-day mechanical demand, losses, topology multipliers, NEC continuous load, generator dynamics, system studies, and utility ride-through profiles [Keentel Engineering — nico3vxC_dA @ 00:19:04].

chapters.question_prompt: What equipment opportunities and adjacent business models do these case studies present, and how do salvage, consignment, sourcing, production, and brokerage differ?
chapters.title: Adjacent Business Models and Equipment Case Studies
chapters.subtitle: Flood salvage, surplus auctions, auction-house ownership, car consignment, junkyards, small production machines, factory vetting, Ghana machinery opportunities, and oil-brokerage claims
chapters.executive_summary: Operators working salvage, surplus, auctions, consignment, finance brokerage, and import deals converge on one playbook: buy or broker equipment the market has mislabeled, and own the buyer network rather than the iron. EquipmentWorld's contractor has run a flood-submerged machine about 2,000 hours after a cheap rebuild; Vantor Surplus shows Code H bulldozers whose fix starts with a $10 filter and takes about half a day; CapitalCode turns a $1,500 F-150 into $4,000 of parts. Plain Finance's auction house stacks a 6% seller fee on a 10% buyer premium, earning $3,200 per $20K machine and $500K in year three. Jermane Cheathem reports $50M+ in brokered equipment deals. SwiftBridge Trading ships excavators only against verified purchase orders on 50/50 terms. The split: Plain Finance lost $150K on a net guarantee, while Flying Wheels refuses $5,000-$6,000 monthly rent and a three-year lease.

sections.title: Section 1: The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: Across salvage yards, military surplus lots, and junkyards, the operators agree that the money in adjacent equipment plays is made on the buy side, by taking iron the market has written off. EquipmentWorld's Wisconsin contractor bought an East Coast machine that was completely submerged when the tunnel pumps quit, paid what they called a definitely cheaper price set by 'your checkbook,' pulled the oil pan, cleaned the underside, chased a few ground issues, replaced the battery wires, and has since run roughly 2,000 hours on it [w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:00:47]. Vantor Surplus describes the same pattern inside government disposal: brand-new bulldozers get coded unserviceable after a lapsed 36-month depot inspection, but storage damage is mostly seals, sulfated batteries, and gummed injectors while internals stay fine, and the fix often starts with a $10 filter because inspectors log units dead without a compression check [lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:05:59]. CapitalCode runs the identical logic at the vehicle level: a wrecked F-150 bought for $1,500 is pulled into $4,000 of parts, netting about $1,400 in operating profit after tow, labor, and other costs [5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:01:54]. The shared rule is that the discount comes from a paperwork or condition label, not from a dead machine.

The second point of agreement is that the durable asset in brokerage, consignment, and auctions is the buyer network, not the inventory. Plain Finance's auction-house operator won a contested job because, in the speaker's words, 'What won the job wasn't a price, but a network he could see,' after building the business on hand-found specialist buyers, honest video, and inspections [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:13:17]. HGreg Lux sells consignment on the same lever: selling yourself means photos, advertising, vetting the buyer, getting a bank to pay a private seller, and paperwork, while selling to a dealer lands below market value, so the consignor's network, multi-platform ads, detailing, and paperwork deliver an agreed net price where the owner 'didn't have to do a thing' [8w7SLSenX5k @ 00:00:49]. Jermane Cheathem, who reports more than $50M in equipment deals as a broker, tells new equipment finance brokers to partner with equipment dealers rather than chase borrowers one by one, and points out the business runs nationwide while mortgage stays local [5RrEsxEZyes @ 00:01:03]. SwiftBridge Trading applies the rule to cross-border iron: no machine ships to Ghana until a verified buyer issues a purchase order, and only then does the shipment follow [XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:16]. The broker's job is matching, and the match comes before the money moves.

The third consensus point is to keep fixed overhead small and verify before committing capital. Flying Wheels' Craig, who has opened three prior dealerships, is restarting in Florida on a shoestring budget under $5,000, refusing $5,000 to $6,000 monthly rent and a three-year lease, saying 'I don't want to just go spend three, four, $5,000 in overhead,' and targeting a shop with seven spots plus bays instead of carrying 30 cars [en-0Xomp1UQ @ 00:13:40]. Lanser Supply builds its whole pitch on vetting rather than owning: 'We don't own the factories,' but every plant is audited before it carries an order, with Zeiss and Hexagon CMM full inspection behind a plus-or-minus 0.002 mm tolerance claim [Vp-CvqpL_ZM @ 00:03:05]. Forgotten Factories Canada shows the downside when the opposite happens on the owner side: at Kelsey-Hayes Windsor, 'Equipment that needed upgrading was patched instead,' overcapacity crept in as a quiet killer, and after the closure the millwrights tagged the equipment that went south to Romulus, Michigan for $8.5M [XuXHM5is32c @ 00:23:09]. The 254,000 sq ft building itself went to Veltri in 1992, which went bankrupt in 2004, before passing to Flex-N-Gate.

sections.title: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Plain Finance lays out the auction-house numbers to the dollar. The operating company was bought for $175K, roughly $110K of it gear, paid as $55K cash plus a $120K seller note running about $2,900 a month for four years, with another $60K added as working capital; the prior owner had handled $3.2M in a year and kept only $22K [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:01:38]. The fee engine is a two-sided take: 'The seller pays us 6%,' and the buyer pays a 10% premium, so a $20K machine earns the house $3,200, and a grinder sold to hand-found specialist buyers hammered at $38K for $6,080 in fees [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:02:57]. Year one ran honest 'Unsold' passes and closed at $4.2M handled and $150K kept; by year three the house ran 10 auctions, handled $7.6M, produced $500K in operating earnings, and refused guarantees after a $520K net guarantee blew up [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:14:31]. Jermane Cheathem frames the finance-side version: equipment finance is the 'wild wild west,' where 'Most states don't require any licensing,' and the broker works a partner stack of underwriters, lenders, and sellers, with the speaker reporting more than $50M in equipment deals [5RrEsxEZyes @ 00:05:27].

The salvage-side mechanics are equally specific. EquipmentWorld's contractor sources from insurance companies and salvagedsale.com, buys underwater units, and passes on burned ones as 'a whole nother challenge,' then schedules the rebuilds for the Wisconsin winter so crews have work in the off-season [w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:01:46]. Vantor Surplus gives the revival sequence for stored dozers: battery disconnect, transfer pump, pilot hose, two 12V batteries in series, and clean diesel, roughly half a day of work, on targets like the D7G and D7R II with 3306 and C9 engines, the Deere 850J, and the Case M4K [lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:09:29]. The same speaker's pre-bid checklist matches the data plate to the DLA catalog, checks for milky fluids, pin bosses, and grouser height, and then reads the demil code: DEMIL A and Q transfer intact, higher codes mean the machine gets torch-cut, and buyers should expect a 50,000-lb lowboy, permits, and an off-highway-only title [lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:12:24]. CapitalCode scales the junkyard version to 40 cars a month at $3,500 each for $140K in revenue; at $2,300 variable cost per car that leaves about $48K contribution and $20K to $30K a month net, with scrap adding $400 to $600 on the F-150 example [5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:07:00].

For cross-border and deal-flow brokering, the workflows are scripted. SwiftBridge Trading's intake captures brand, model, weight, engine, bucket, hours, and budget before sourcing, and works three machine tiers of 20 to 22 ton, 30 to 36 ton, and 45-ton-plus, with refurbished units also on the table, against a Ghana market that imported about US$205M of excavators in 2023 [XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:39]. Its payment terms run 50% against a copy of the bill of lading and 50% within 15 days of arrival at Tema, varying deal by deal, and the stated expansion path after machines is parts, service, then rental and leasing [XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:06:06]. Alex Zastre applies the same broker logic to oil: research the sector with GPT, build lists in Apollo, send a cold-email template, and close on a discovery call, charging $35K upfront for a year-long engagement plus a per-deal fee that runs 1%, or $500K on a $50M deal and $5M on a $500M deal [9EgxHbU-ajg @ 00:03:14]. Easy Business prices the service-machine version: an $8,500 laser rust remover billed at $40 to $60 per part or $70 to $90 an hour, with three to four jobs a day producing about $200 or more [SSM9tqoMGu4 @ 00:05:23].

callout.body: Four small moves the operators credit for keeping salvage, surplus, auction, and dealership plays profitable and out of trouble.
items: Schedule salvage rebuilds for the dead season: 'you need to have something for the guys to do in the winter so we'll go through it and fix it and get it operational again' [EquipmentWorld — w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:02:03].
'Read the demil code first' before bidding on surplus iron: DEMIL A and Q transfer intact, while higher codes mean the machine gets torch-cut [Vantor Surplus — lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:12:24].
Keep consignor money off your operating books: 'The sellers' proceeds never touch your account,' so they cannot cover your payroll or a guarantee shortfall [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:11:48].

sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest split is whether you own the iron or own the relationship. Lanser Supply runs a pure vetting model: “We don’t own the factories,” yet it routes one purchase order across 70+ CNC machines with 6 m beds and audits every plant before that plant carries an order [Vp-CvqpL_ZM @ 00:03:05]. Jermane Cheathem argues the same asset-light logic from the finance side, telling brokers to partner with equipment dealers rather than chase borrowers, because equipment finance runs nationwide while mortgage stays local [5RrEsxEZyes @ 00:01:03]. CapitalCode pushes back with an owner’s balance sheet: a junkyard sitting on a $1M property producing $300k a year must subtract roughly $100k a year in land opportunity cost before anyone calls it profitable [5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:04:47]. Flying Wheels lands in the middle. Craig, a three-time dealership founder, is restarting in Florida on a shoestring budget, refusing $5,000-to-$6,000 monthly rent and a three-year lease, and says flatly, “I don’t want to just go spend three, four, $5,000 in overhead” [en-0Xomp1UQ @ 00:13:40]. The operator read: ownership buys margin control and inventory depth, while brokering and vetting buy speed and geographic reach, and each camp treats the other camp’s fixed costs as the main risk to survival.

Fee structure is the second fault line: commission on someone else’s asset versus taking principal risk. HGreg Lux sells consignment as the escape from two bad options, since selling yourself means photos, ads, buyer vetting, getting a bank to pay a private seller and paperwork, while selling to a dealer means a below-market number; consignors get an agreed net price and “didn’t have to do a thing” [8w7SLSenX5k @ 00:00:49]. Plain Finance’s auction-house case runs the commission stack explicitly: the seller pays 6% and the buyer pays a 10% premium, so a $20K machine earns $3,200, and by year three the house refused guarantees outright [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:02:57]. SwiftBridge Trading refuses to speculate on stock at all, sequencing verified buyer, then purchase order, then shipment, with 50% paid against a bill-of-lading copy and 50% within 15 days of arrival at Tema [XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:16]. Alex Zastre goes furthest toward getting paid before any deal closes, charging $35k upfront for a year-long engagement plus a per-deal broker fee, and Zastre pegs the back end at 1%, meaning $500k on a $50M deal and $5M on a $500M deal [9EgxHbU-ajg @ 00:02:11].

The third split is salvage-and-repair versus buy-new-and-produce. EquipmentWorld’s Wisconsin contractor sources fully submerged units from insurance companies and salvagedsale.com, prices them off “your checkbook,” and has logged about 2,000 hours on one flood unit since repair, but draws a hard line at burned machines, calling them “a whole nother challenge” [w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:01:46]. Vantor Surplus makes the same contrarian bet on Pentagon disposals, arguing that stored condition-coded dozers often need only a battery disconnect, transfer pump, pilot hose, two 12V batteries in series and clean diesel, roughly half a day of work [lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:09:29]. The buy-new camp starts from a catalog instead. Garage Profits lists a $300 plastic shredder through a $2,200 Styrofoam densifier and argues “you’re not selling trash, you’re selling raw material,” yet posts no earnings figures [InQ7-NaPvxs @ 00:01:36]. Easy Business gives harder unit math: a CNC wood lathe turns $0.60 of cost into a $2-to-$5 piece, an $8,500 laser rust remover bills $40 to $60 per part, and a $650-to-$1,000 sublimation setup pays back after about 300 mugs in one to two months [SSM9tqoMGu4 @ 00:01:37]. Salvage players trade mechanical labor for discount; machine buyers trade capital for repeatable output.

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive failure on record is the net guarantee. In Plain Finance’s auction-house case, the operator guaranteed a seller $520K net with no reserves, leaning on $620K in comps, three qualified inspections and $165K in cash, on terms that paid a 12% premium plus any upside, minus $50K in event costs [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:06:18]. The best machine carried $190K comps and hammered at $84K, the sale totaled $375K, and the $145K shortfall cost the house $150K, leaving $15K against a $9K payroll, with seller proceeds “not one dollar” usable because “the sellers’ proceeds never touch your account” [9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:11:48]. The lesson the narrator draws is brutal: comps are not bidders, and “Two is a market.” Recovery came from refusing to cover an $11K reserve gap and winning jobs on a visible network rather than price. Forgotten Factories Canada shows the slow version of the same arithmetic at Kelsey-Hayes Windsor: “Equipment that needed upgrading was patched instead,” overcapacity became “a quiet killer,” and the plant closed with 15 days’ notice before its equipment went to Romulus, Michigan for $8.5M [XuXHM5is32c @ 00:23:09]. Both cases punish operators who let fixed obligations outrun real, present demand.

Condition and buying discipline decide whether cheap iron stays cheap. CapitalCode shows how wide the spread runs: Yard A turns a $150k buying budget into $350k in sales while Yard B turns the same $150k into $220k, and the gap comes entirely from what each yard chose to buy [5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:06:05]. The same breakdown flags luxury cars with damaged electronics and EV batteries as the inventory that wrecks returns [5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:06:43]. Vantor Surplus warns that government inspectors log stored units dead without running a compression check, so the buyer’s edge is real, but the trap is the DEMIL code: A and Q transfer intact, higher codes mean torch-cut, and even a clean dozer demands a 50,000-lb lowboy, permits and an off-highway-only title, which is why the rule is “Read the demil code first” [lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:12:24]. EquipmentWorld’s flood unit still needed the oil pan pulled, battery wires replaced and “a few ground issues” chased down before it earned its 2,000 hours [w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:01:29]. The Wood Whisperer adds a finishing-side caution: the heated linseed, beeswax and carnauba blend is not durable, and spot repairs can become an eyesore [87nsgCs4Tzs @ 00:12:08].

Operational bottlenecks hit before the first sale. Flying Wheels walked Florida’s licensing chain from town hall to the Martin County dealer desk in Stuart to the regional FLHSMV office in West Palm, which books appointments only by phone from 8 to noon and hung up twice, then bounced the call to a compliance officer’s voicemail at what Craig calls step three [en-0Xomp1UQ @ 00:09:23]. The New Hampshire compliance officer Craig dealt with earlier was strict enough that visits felt like audits. SwiftBridge Trading lists the import-side breakpoints as payment, quality, port clearance, FX and after-sales, plus a hard refusal to sell to galamsey buyers as tracking and import controls tighten [XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:10:21]. Keentel Engineering shows the same choke point at utility scale: missing dynamic models produce “a hard schedule stop,” cogeneration means “if the turbine goes down, your cooling might go down with it,” and OEM diligence has to pin contractual delivery dates, lifecycle cost and 2028 service depth [UxhrvcRGfdc @ 00:11:20]. Even adoption eats time; EquipmentWorld’s crew fought satellite and Bluetooth-to-rover-header problems for about six months before GPS became something they “wouldn’t really go without” [w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:02:59].

callout.title: Gate Every Deal Before Capital Moves
callout.body: Each gate below comes straight from a loss, a near-miss, or a hard rule a practitioner learned on the floor, the yard, or the dock.
items: Refuse net guarantees without reserves; $620K in comps produced a $375K sale and a $150K hit to the house [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:06:18].
Match the data plate to the DLA catalog and check for milky fluids, pin bosses and grouser height before bidding on surplus [Vantor Surplus — lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:11:28].
Buy underwater units from insurers and salvagedsale.com but skip burned machines entirely [EquipmentWorld — w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:01:46].
Lock a verified buyer and purchase order before shipping heavy iron, and refuse galamsey buyers outright [SwiftBridge Trading LLP — XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:16].

action_checklist: Walk into local dealerships and introduce yourself in person to surface location leads and shared-lot options [Flying Wheels — en-0Xomp1UQ @ 00:11:56].
Partner with equipment dealers as your referral engine instead of chasing individual borrowers, and work the nationwide market [Jermane Cheathem — 5RrEsxEZyes @ 00:01:03].
Run a full spec intake on every buyer request: brand, model, weight, engine, bucket, hours and budget [SwiftBridge Trading LLP — XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:39].
Source flood-damaged units from insurers and salvagedsale.com and schedule the rebuilds for winter so crews stay busy [EquipmentWorld — w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:02:03].
Hunt specialist buyers by hand with an honest video and open inspections; one grinder hammered at $38K and earned $6,080 in fees [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:03:17].
Build outbound with GPT research, Apollo lists, a cold-email template and a discovery-call close [Alex Zastre — 9EgxHbU-ajg @ 00:03:14].
